package pbkdf2 // import "golang.org/x/crypto/pbkdf2"

Package pbkdf2 implements the key derivation function PBKDF2 as defined in RFC
2898 / PKCS #5 v2.0.

A key derivation function is useful when encrypting data based on a password
or any other not-fully-random data. It uses a pseudorandom function to derive a
secure encryption key based on the password.

While v2.0 of the standard defines only one pseudorandom function to use,
HMAC-SHA1, the drafted v2.1 specification allows use of all five FIPS Approved
Hash Functions SHA-1, SHA-224, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 for HMAC. To choose,
you can pass the `New` functions from the different SHA packages to pbkdf2.Key.

func Key(password, salt []byte, iter, keyLen int, h func() hash.Hash) []byte

  - [`NewEncryptor`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-mwbwe6bu/encryption/encryption.go#L35-L43) validates 32-byte keys and wraps [`ErrInvalidKey`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-mwbwe6bu/encryption/encryption.go#L29) otherwise.
  - [`Encryptor.EncryptWriter`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-mwbwe6bu/encryption/encryption.go#L45-L64) streams AES-256-GCM chunks up to 64KB with the 3-byte header (`0x4F 0x44 0x01`), 4-byte big-endian chunk length prefix (`nonce + ciphertext + tag`), unique 12-byte random nonces per chunk, 4-byte zero sentinel, and 32-byte HMAC-SHA256 trailer over all bytes between header and sentinel, with idempotent `Close()`.
  - [`DecryptReader`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-mwbwe6bu/encryption/encryption.go#L179-L204) lazily initializes on `Read`, verifying header magic (`"invalid header"`), version (`"unsupported version"`), chunk authentication/truncation, and trailing HMAC (`"integrity"`).
